title: Hear, O Israel (Deuteronomy 6:4–9)
hookLine: love the Lord with all thy heart, soul and strength; Jesus calls it the first commandment

lines: ONE SENTENCE, PRAYED TWICE A DAY.
cards: Forty years have passed. The generation that left Egypt is almost gone. Israel is camped on the plains of Moab, across the Jordan from the land, and Moses, old now, gives one long last speech: the book of Deuteronomy.

In the middle of it he says one sentence so central that it's been prayed every morning and every night for many centuries. When Jesus is asked which commandment is the greatest of all, he doesn't make up a new answer.

teach.b: First, the word. It begins with a command: "Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God is one Lord." In Hebrew, the first word is shema, hear, and that's what the whole prayer is called.
Not believe, not think about. Hear. Listening is where it starts.

"Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart, and with thy whole soul, and with thy whole strength." Heart, in Hebrew thinking, is where you decide, not only where you feel. Soul is your life itself.
And strength is a word that usually means very or exceedingly: love God with all your muchness, everything you've got. Third, the places. These words shall be in your heart, Moses says.

teach.h: AT HOME, ON THE ROAD, ON THE DOOR.
teach.b: Talk about them at home and on the road, lying down and getting up. Bind them on your hand and between your eyes; write them on the doorposts.
Jews still do this: the small scroll on the doorframe, the mezuzah, and the leather boxes called tefillin worn in morning prayer.
They still pray the Shema morning and night; for many, it is the last thing they hope to say. Fourth, Jesus.

When a scribe asks him which commandment is first of all, Jesus answers, in Mark's Gospel, beginning with these same words, hear, O Israel, and then adds a second from Leviticus: love your neighbor as yourself.

In Matthew he calls the first the greatest. Catholics pray the Shema too. Every Saturday night, the Church's Night Prayer reads these verses from Deuteronomy, at the very hour Moses names: when you lie down.

how: In the Liturgy of the Hours, Night Prayer on Saturday evening includes Deuteronomy 6:4–7, and the Catechism opens its teaching on the first commandment with Jesus's words, love the Lord your God with all your heart.

games.q: you're a scribe in Jerusalem. you've been listening to Jesus debate, and he's answered well. you ask him: which commandment is the first of all? what does he say?
o: hear, O Israel: love the Lord thy God with all thy heart.
games.why: he quotes the Shema from Deuteronomy, then adds a second: love your neighbor as yourself. no other commandment is greater than these.

practice: Start where the prayer starts: for a minute, just listen, to the room, your breath, the silence underneath.
Then, if you pray, say the words slowly: Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God is one Lord; thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart, and with thy whole soul, and with thy whole strength.
If you don't pray, ask instead what you love with your whole heart.

wordCard.voice: Shema. Hebrew for hear: the first word of Israel's great prayer, love God with heart, soul and strength, which Jesus called the first commandment. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: hear, listen. the first word of Deuteronomy 6:4, and the name of the whole prayer.

carryVoice: Your line: with all thy heart. First hear, then love. Day three hundred eighty-seven, done.
